terms.comment: A phrase from a Roman board game: incitae (calcēs) are pieces that can no longer move (Isid. Orig. 18.67). Plautus uses it of a person cornered; Hofmann (1698) and Morgan–Owens take it for checkmate.
Traupman gives it for the call “checkmate!”, but “look out for your king” is the warning of check.

phrases.latin: Profectō ad incitās lēnōnem rediget, sī eās abdūxerit.
phrases.english: He’ll certainly checkmate the pimp, if he gets those girls away.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 51, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. checkmate, mate (vb.).
